title: Tooling: schedule isolated test modules concurrently with identical receipts (3.3-3.9x faster verify-tests, no new kappa)
body:
## Tooling: schedule isolated test modules concurrently with identical receipts

Status: **tooling improvement** (verification engineering, track 85–94, assignment seed 88). No new kappa claim. Prepared with help from opencode.

### What and why

`scripts/run_isolated_tests.py` (run by `make verify-tests`, hence `make verify`) runs every test module in a fresh interpreter to isolate colliding research-package module names. A timing survey of the `make verify` checks at base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631` found this runner to be the single most expensive check: 298.5 s end to end (and over a 250 s sweep budget), while every other surveyed check was at most 144 s (`scripts/audit_quadratic_affine.py`), most under 10 s. No open PR (surveyed 703) targets the test runner or generic parallelism.

The runner now schedules the same per-module commands concurrently — one isolated interpreter per module; `--workers N` pins the width — and replays each module's captured bytes in sorted module order. The isolation design is unchanged; it is exactly what makes the modules independent and safely concurrent. A test-module audit found no writes outside `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` blocks, so concurrent modules share no mutable state.

### Measured result (same host, same input, 16 logical CPUs, CPython 3.13.15/Windows)

| Run | Modules | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-change runner, base commit, end to end | 87 | 298.5 s |
| Benchmark sequential pass (pre-change schedule) | 88 | 250.6 s |
| Benchmark concurrent pass (16 workers) | 88 | 75.9 s (3.30x) |
| Post-change runner end to end | 88 | 76.7 s (3.9x vs base) |

### Exactness (machine-checked, `research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/benchmark.py`)

Per-module command is byte-identical to the pre-change one (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <module> -v`, same interpreter/cwd/env); only scheduling changes. Across 88 modules:

- exit codes identical for all 88; the failing-module sets of both schedules are equal (same 15 environmental Windows failures, e.g. `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'resource'`, present identically at base);
- stdout byte-identical for all 88; stderr byte-identical for 87 modulo the wall-clock field `unittest -v` embeds in `Ran N tests in T.TTTs`;
- `test_frontier799_bindings.py` is inherently nondeterministic across any two runs (its failing traceback embeds a machine-random temp path). The benchmark proves this automatically by re-running any mismatched module twice under the same schedule: `scheduling_driven_mismatches` is empty.

No certificate, patch, generator, proof supplement or hash-pinned source file is touched (`run_isolated_tests.py` is not pinned by `certificates/selected-result.json`, `SELECTED-SOURCE.json` or any checkpoint).

### Negative controls

`tests/test_isolated_test_runner.py` runs the real runner end to end in a sandbox: (1) a deliberately failing module must appear in the shared `Failed modules:` summary; (2) a barrier test — three modules each wait (8 s) for three markers, passing only if at least three module processes run concurrently — fails against the pre-change runner with "barrier timeout: test modules did not run concurrently" and passes with `--workers 3` after; (3) default-invocation summary lines and exit codes are unchanged.

### Reproduce

    python3 -B research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/benchmark.py

Expected final line: `PASS identical exit codes (88 modules); receipts identical for 87 modules modulo the unittest timing field; 1 module(s) inherently nondeterministic across same-mode runs: ['test_frontier799_bindings.py']`

On a Unix host `python3 -B scripts/run_isolated_tests.py` should end `PASS all 88 test modules in isolated interpreters`; on this Windows host it exits 1 with the same 15-module environmental failing set as at base (documented in the package README).

### Scope and remaining obligations

Windows portability of the 15 pre-existing failing modules is out of scope; the claim is exact reproduction of the sequential runner's receipts, exit codes and failing set. Live interleaved output is replaced by sorted per-module replay. Related concurrent tooling on a different target: PR #853 ([PR 741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/741) pinned-stage concurrency) — independent of and not depended on by this change. Base commit, claim record and full evidence are in `research/agent-07-verifeng-seed88/` (README.md, SPRINT-CLAIM.md, evidence/benchmark.json).
